ca_shadow_play_boulder.blurb: A small bouldering spot on the east rim above the Happy Boulders canyon near Bishop, with eleven problems in all. The spread is wide for so few lines: a couple of V0s and V2s, a handful in the V3 to V4 range, then a steeper set from V6 up to a single V7. You can pick between sun and shade. The gentler problems sit high above the canyon floor and feel airy, while the harder ones are shorter and steeper in a cooler cave-like pocket. The area as a whole catches afternoon sun, which makes it a good end-of-day stop. Reach it by taking the rim trail up from the main Happy Boulders hike.

ca_train_time_wall.blurb: A small, lightly visited wall on Donner Summit, perched above the old railroad tunnels near the I-80 corridor west of Lake Tahoe. Most of the eleven routes are gear climbs, with two bolted lines mixed in. Grades start around 5.7 and 5.8, bulk up in the 5.10 range, and top out with one 5.11. It makes a decent choice when you want shade or want to avoid the busier Donner Summit crags. Expect single-pitch cracks, corners and short faces rather than long outings.

ca_housekeeping_boulder_the.blurb: One of the better-regarded single boulders in Yosemite Valley, part of the Housekeeping bouldering zone beside the campground and its LeConte memorial building. It holds eleven problems with a broad spread: a few V0 to V1 lines, several at V2 to V3, a couple around V5, and one much harder problem near V8. Granodiorite features include crimps, jugs and small crystals for feet, with lock-off cruxes and jug top-outs. A short walk from the road makes it easy to combine with the other boulders nearby, and it suits a mixed group of warm-up and project climbers.

ca_sugar_cookie_the.blurb: A compact crag in the Lower Merced River Canyon of Yosemite, set just left of the Cookie Sheet and reached by the same approach. It has eleven routes, split fairly evenly between bolted lines and gear climbs. This is hard-climber territory: one 5.10 serves as the warm-up, and nearly everything else runs from 5.12 into 5.13. The base is a flat staging spot below three separate bolted lines. The wall gets sun early and goes into shade in the afternoon. Watch for poison oak on the walk in and at the base.

_expect.name: Cirque of the Climbables - Left Side

ca_cirque_of_the_climbables_left_side.blurb: The left half of a cirque high on the south face of Queen Mountain in Joshua Tree National Park, among the more reachable crags on that mountain. All eleven routes are traditional, with the odd one doubling as a top-rope. Grades run from 5.8 up to 5.11, centred firmly on 5.10, so it rewards climbers who are comfortable leading that range on rock coated in dark desert varnish. A few lines are runout, and the walk to the base is a solid effort on a cairned trail.

ca_trojan_boulder.blurb: A roadside boulder at Painted Cave in the mountains above Santa Barbara, set alone on the west side of the road and overhanging it enough that passing vehicles have scraped the top. It carries eleven problems. Easy options at V0 make it friendly to newcomers, the middle of the range holds V2 to V4 lines, and a few harder ones reach V6, V8 and V9. Height is modest, mostly short to mid-sized. It sits only minutes from town, so it is an easy after-work session, and the other Painted Cave boulders are a few steps away.

ca_underworld_rock.blurb: A shady sandstone crag tucked in a ravine below Castle Rock, in the Castle Rock State Park area. Eleven routes mix mostly bolted sport lines with a few gear climbs, many on moderate slab that is easy to top-rope from the anchors. Grades range from 5.8 through 5.9, a handful of 5.10s, and several 5.11s. The rock is pocketed with huecos, so there is usually a hold nearby. Expect a steep, sandy and slippery descent in, and a quieter, cool-feeling spot compared with the more popular rocks nearby.
